size_pct_nav: 0; no Berkshire Microsoft position documented in the review window

drivers.driver: Buffett did not understand Microsoft's business well enough to underwrite it despite admiring its success.
drivers.quote: I don't worry about not buying Microsoft, though, because I didn't understand that business.

drivers.driver: The relevant skill is identifying predictable economics, not benefiting from every successful technology company.
Avoiding technology forecasts outside his circle was discipline, not a negative prediction about the company's products.

entry_valuation_stated: Strong financial control case; exact March 1 price/multiple unrecovered. PASS reason is outside circle, not proof that shares were overvalued.
outcome_note: Documented refusal, not a silently inferred nonholding. Later friendship/conflict explanations must not replace the pre-cutoff circle-of-competence explanation. The July 1998 conversation also discloses Buffett's personal 100-share tracking purchase; this is a Berkshire deployment PASS, not a claim that Buffett personally never owned one share.
sources: Microsoft fiscal 1998 annual financial highlights, https://www.microsoft.com/investor/reports/ar98/fins.htm ; January 19, 1999 earnings announcement; pre-cutoff antitrust proceedings; https://news.microsoft.com/source/1999/01/19/microsoft-announces-record-quarterly-revenue-and-income-3; fund reference https://www.berkshirehathaway.com/letters/1998htm.html
pack_quality_notes: Pre-cutoff refusal verified in full dated transcript mirror of Fortune's 'The Bill & Warren Show', July 20, 1998 (original archive https://money.cnn.com/magazines/fortune/fortune_archive/1998/07/20/245683/). The same conversation mentions a personal 100-share tracking purchase, explicitly not Berkshire portfolio ownership. No complete historical 13F archive recovered; annual major-holdings evidence plus the refusal supports the window control, not an all-time exhaustive negative. March quote missing.
